item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption examines how agencies can strengthen invoice-payment controls while managing costs and processing times.
item.support: seeks to present approaches to the design and management of the payment process

item.text: Its research includes responses from 150 state and local government organisations and consultation across public, private and non-profit sectors.
item.support: The methodology and summary analysis of 150 survey respondents are presented in the appendix.

item.text: The Commission reports that gaps in payment controls have enabled corruption, including through weak processes and pressure on accounts payable staff.
item.support: Commission investigations have shown that corrupt conduct is able to occur because of gaps in invoice payment control.

item.text: The Commission proposes five strategies covering staff capability, supplier records, payment-process design, consistent processing and informed expenditure review.
item.support: The Commission has identified the following five strategies for tightening the payment process.

item.quote: The solution is not a simple matter of applying more careful checks, further segregating duties or removing discretionary decision-making.
